solved_evidence: T067 is absent from ROWS.jsonl; assumed scope is KS tightness for q=3 and ferromagnetic q=4 symmetric channels, including regular/Galton–Watson trees and the SBM. Mossel–Sly–Sohn (2022 preprint; Ann. Probab. 2025), Theorems 1.5 and 1.12, pp. 3 and 5 of arXiv v2, settle sufficiently large degrees. Their Theorem 1.13 proves non-tightness for q>=5 and for antiferromagnetic q=4 at sufficiently small degrees; KS tightness without these qualifications is false. https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.03362

frontier.title: Exact Phase Transitions for Stochastic Block Models and Reconstruction on Trees
frontier.authors: Elchanan Mossel, Allan Sly, Youngtak Sohn

condition: “if d ≥ d₀ and dλ² ≤ 1” — Mossel–Sly–Sohn, arXiv:2212.03362v2, Theorem 1.5, p. 3. No numerical value of d₀ is supplied. Theorem 1.12, p. 5, is the corresponding Galton–Watson statement under Assumptions 1.10–1.11.
obstruction: Section 5 replaces the log-posterior recursion by a Gaussian recursion with an error vanishing as d→∞; this drives the magnetization into the region controlled by the Taylor expansion. At small d the Gaussian approximation error need not be dominated by the negative drift, especially for q=4 where the quadratic term vanishes and the leading drift is cubic.
compute_plan: First make every normal-approximation, small-magnetization, and remainder constant effective, then seek certified contraction for the remaining degrees and lambda intervals. Appendix B, pp. 50–54, already proves g₄(s)<s using a Taylor bound and finite numerical integration; recertifying its grid (equations 135–140) verifies an ingredient of an existing theorem, not the open small-degree extension.
compute_size: Unknown for the open problem. The appendix gives quadrature grids n=200 or 100 on a three-dimensional truncated Gaussian domain, so its existing certificate is reproducible but can be expensive. No finite list of unresolved degrees is specified.
risks: Theorem 1.12 covers whole offspring-law families; that domain is infinite-dimensional. Poisson/SBM average degree d is real, so small d is also a continuum. General-tree extensions are different unsolved questions. q=4 antiferromagnetic KS tightness is false below the explicit threshold d* (about 22.2694 for Poisson, 24.408 for regular offspring). Exact T067 statement missing.
